correctness.rationale: For constant functions the defining multiplicative derivative is constant and each further derivative squares it. Thus the matrix-valued uniformity norm restricts exactly to the normalized Schatten norm of exponent \(q=2^k\). The explicit two-coordinate diagonal pair has unit norm, distance \(\varepsilon\), and midpoint norm \((1-(\varepsilon/2)^q)^{1/q}\), producing the upper bound. Corollary 4.2 of arXiv:2606.16862v2 gives the same quantity as a lower bound for the full space. This proves equality for all stated parameters. The finite verifier checks sample instances but is not used as the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The primary source makes uniform convexity a central geometric consequence of its matrix-valued Hanner inequality but leaves the modulus as a lower bound. The exact modulus is a natural global invariant: it quantifies the best possible midpoint stability and proves that the source estimate cannot be improved by exploiting group or noncommutative cube structure. The saturation mechanism is structural, occurring in an isometric normalized Schatten sector of constant functions, and the statement is complete for every finite group, every matrix size at least two and every uniformity order at least two.
